subject: Literature
title: Julius Caesar and Political Assassination
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Julius Caesar and Political Assassination.

hook.text: Brutus kills his best friend to save the Roman Republic and discovers that good intentions lead to chaos.

buildup.text: Shakespeare's Julius Caesar explores whether political assassination can ever be morally justified.

discovery.text: Mark Antony's funeral speech, 'Friends, Romans, countrymen,' showed how rhetoric can weaponize grief.

twist.text: The play was dangerously topical: Elizabeth I had no heir, and assassination plots were a constant threat.

climax.text: Julius Caesar remains required reading for understanding how political violence spirals beyond anyone's control.

punchline.text: Killing a tyrant created something worse than tyranny.

quiz.question: What does Mark Antony's funeral speech demonstrate?
options: How rhetoric can manipulate crowds and weaponize grief
